documents.body: .. / tee File write File write This executable can write data to local files. Comment Use -a to append data to exising files. Remarks If there are environment variables involved, they must be passed via sudo VAR=value ... or exported then sudo -E ... . echo DATA | tee /path/to/output-file SUID This function is performed by the privileged user if the executable has the SUID bit set and the right ownership because the effective privileges are not dropped. echo DATA | tee /path/to/output-file

requests.query: GTFOBins sudo overwrite a local file
requests.information_need: Find an example that can replace existing local file contents under sudo.
requests.rule: Requires an actual write replacing content under sudo. Append-only, deletion and mere truncation do not qualify.

requests.query: GTFOBins unprivileged overwrite an existing file
requests.information_need: Replace a chosen existing local file with selected content as a normal user.
requests.rule: Must document writing chosen content that replaces a selected existing local file in the requested privilege context. Append-only, deleting, merely truncating, unrelated preparation, and unspecified effect do not count. A documented overwrite option on that example qualifies.

requests.query: GTFOBins alternatives for appending text to a file with sudo
requests.information_need: Find other sources for appending local text under sudo.
requests.rule: Only non-GTFOBins documents with substantive append-to-file and sudo evidence qualify.

requests.query: alternatives to GTFOBins for appending a line to a file under sudo
requests.information_need: Find other sources for privileged append of selected local text.
requests.rule: Only non-GTFOBins documentation. Must give a substantive example adding selected text at the end of a local file while preserving previous contents, with sudo applied to the actual writer. An unrelated sudo command, append without sudo, and a shell redirect outside sudo do not qualify.
